page: Microsoft Azure E112ias_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V. The server is powered by dedicated x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processors operating at 3.525 GHz, providing 112 vCPUs across 56 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The system features 672.0 GB of memory, representing a ratio of 6.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache specifications include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. Cryptographic extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, alongside AVX, BMI2, and ADX, although AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The instance does not include bundled local storage or bundled complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing capabilities driven by the high core count. The server scored 151,080.86 on stress-ng multi-core testing and reached 566.51 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, placing both metrics in the top 10% tier. Cryptographic performance is particularly notable, with a PassMark CPU encryption score of 119,178.14 (top 10%). Geekbench multi-core testing reached 18,671.0, with specific sub-tests showing top 10% results in ray tracing (96,986.0) and image processing (17,737.0). In-memory database workloads also perform well, as shown by PassMark database operations at 26,336.5 and Redis SET operations exceeding 101.62 million operations per second.

Single-thread performance and uncached memory operations register in the middle tiers. Stress-ng single-core scored 2,893.09, and Geekbench single-core produced 1,721.0. While small-block cached memory bandwidth achieved 6,716.89 GB/sec (top 25%), large-block uncached read and write bandwidths reached 126.71 GB/sec and 62.78 GB/sec respectively. Large language model inference speeds fall within average to strong percentiles depending on model parameters, reaching 182.94 prompt tokens per second and 28.3 generation tokens per second on medium 7B models, but dropping to 3.04 generation tokens per second on large 70B models.

Cost efficiency is centered on high-density CPU parallelization and substantial RAM capacity within an isolated environment. The absence of local disk requires external storage volume provisioning, which must be considered in architectural sizing. Microsoft Azure E112ias_v5 is well positioned for enterprise in-memory databases, large-scale caching layers, software compilation, data analytics pipelines, and heavily parallel computational tasks that do not depend on specialized vector acceleration instructions.
description: Microsoft Azure E112ias_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized instance featuring 112 dedicated vCPUs and 56 physical cores from an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. It provides 672.0 GB of RAM (6.0 GB per core) and operates on Microsoft Hyper-V without integrated local storage or GPUs. Benchmark data demonstrates exceptional multi-threaded performance, ranking in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core (151,080.86), PassMark encryption (119,178.14), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (566.51 GB/sec). Memory benchmarks highlight strong cached read throughput alongside robust key-value performance, achieving over 101.62 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread speeds and uncached memory bandwidth fall into the median range, the instance offers dense computing capacity and large memory allocation. It is architecturally suited for large-scale enterprise databases, distributed caching layers, software build environments, and data engineering workloads.
